about.operatorText:
POCKET MONkEY is self-hosted software, not a hosting or managed service provided by the project. The instance operator is the person or organisation deploying and controlling this installation. Project maintainers and ordinary household users are not automatically its operator; an application's Manager role alone does not determine who has legal responsibility for a deployment.

The operator is responsible for appropriate hosting, network exposure and HTTPS, access control, configuration, persistent storage, confidential backups and tested recovery, and installation of application, dependency and host security updates. Restrict access to intended users. LAN or VPN access does not remove the need to assess these protections. Backups must include the database, account images and persistent authentication keys, with the configuration needed to restore the installation correctly.

The project supplies software, not an availability commitment, monitoring service, maintenance contract or recovery service. A separately arranged service is governed by its own agreement, not implied by use of POCKET MONkEY.

about.privacyText:
This installation processes information needed to manage access and shared pocket-money records. This includes usernames and display names, authentication and session/security records, language and theme preferences, account names and images, balances, transaction amounts/dates/comments and recorded attribution, and monthly-allowance settings and execution records. Do not enter unnecessary personal or sensitive information into names, images or comments.

Managers can read all accounts. Members can read only active accounts assigned to them by a Manager. Accounts remain shared instance resources, not individually owned private spaces. Host administrators and parties with storage or backup access may have access outside the application's role controls.

Browser cookies support authentication, request security and language selection. Connecting to an installation also exposes technical request information to its host and, where used, its reverse proxy. Application/host logs and backups may contain additional information depending on configuration. Hosting providers or other integrations are the operator's deployment choices, not a hosted service supplied by the project. Using the software does not automatically send household records to project maintainers; sharing diagnostics or bug reports can disclose data, so review and redact them first.

The operator determines the installation's purposes, access, hosting and backup practices and must assess applicable privacy obligations. This general software description is not a complete privacy notice for every deployment. Ask the instance operator for the installation's contact details and, where applicable, information about legal basis, recipients, storage locations, transfers, retention and your rights. No particular legal basis or exemption is assumed.

Transaction-detail retention defaults to 24 UTC calendar months and can be configured by the operator. Cleanup removes eligible older transaction details, not all associated data: balances, opening entries, audit information and durable processing identities remain. Disabling a user prevents access but is not data erasure. Backups may retain earlier copies; increasing the retention period does not recover details already removed. This setting is not a promise of automatic deletion or anonymisation of all personal information. Any applicable request or retention obligation needs deployment-specific assessment by the operator.
